programmes.show_description: Glen tackles Jack's inking, Sketch rids Ben of a silly spooning tattoo, Alice waves her magic wand for Kamila, and Jay fixes Matt's backside-based chat-up line.
Chris Ramsey draws the line at dried spaghetti, the comics are shaken and stirred by a big tube, and Judi Love 'impresses' the Taskmaster with her life achievements.
Jimmy Carr hosts as Jon Richardson and Jo Brand take on Joe Wilkinson and Jamali Maddix. Rachel Parris joins Susie Dent in Dictionary Corner. With Rachel Riley.

Teleshopping
Ashley and Brandon Wright, the co-owners of Hamburger Mary's, go incognito in their company, to ensure that their culture of diversity is being maintained as the business grows.
Dan Duffy, CEO of the United Real Estate Group, goes undercover in his own firm. He meets different employees and learns about their professional and personal lives.
...Selling: Nurse Jenna and firefighter Neil need to sell his frat house before they can settle down in their own home. Can the place be revived and smoke out the competition?
In Devon, there's a 'Britalian' mash-up, stomach-churning confessions and generous helpings of criticism, as three rival couples put their hosting skills to the ultimate test.
In Hull, image-conscious Jay and Heather go all-out American. Thrifty Mike and Stef serve a school dinner throwback. And is Steve and Stephanie's fine dining fare a little too fancy?
The Big Fat Nigerian One: Ola's handed over control of her wedding to super-cool groom Raphael, who's looking to plan a gigantic Nigerian wedding for the ages.
The Romeo and Juliet One: Dan plans to prove his romantic prowess by organising a Shakespearean wedding in Italy for Kate. He's hoping for a happier ending than the play he's inspired by...
Mike Roper, the president and CEO of quick-service Tex-Mex restaurant chain Taco Bueno, disguises himself to work among his staff and gain insight before growing the business.
John Carona, CEO of property management company Associa, goes undercover in his own organisation to see first-hand how his employees are dealing with recent changes at the firm.
Lido Di Manhattan: Ambitious graduate Lisa bought her restaurant in California at just 23 but, five years later, she's worried she picked the wrong venture. Can Gordon help?
Anna Vincenzo's: Gordon Ramsay visits Italian restaurant Anna Vincenzo's in Florida, where owner CeCe has lost her way in the kitchen. But can she take constructive criticism?
...and Selling: Brand new series: Paul and Julie are parents feeling the squeeze. As well as wanting to size up, they need to keep their mortgage to a minimum. Can the twins help?
Royal Rumble: Ben's wandering eyes upset Sunny. There's major drama when new guests are royally demanding. And Fraser reaches breaking point with Barbie.
Taskmaster Greg Davies delivers rough justice as Ardal O'Hanlon sings about a fence, Judi Love designs classy headgear, and Sophie Duker displays world-class endurance.
Sean Lock, Bob Mortimer, Harry Hill, Joe Lycett, Jon Richardson, Lucy Beaumont, Katherine Ryan and more take on the words and numbers in this best-bits compilation episode.
Sean Lock, Bob Mortimer, Jon Richardson, Lucy Beaumont, Rosie Jones, Victoria Coren-Mitchell and more take on the words and numbers in this best-bits compilation episode.
A Beautiful Mind: Jeremy tries to impress Zahra by holding a book group, but he's only ever read Mr Nice. Meanwhile, Mark is worried that he can't satisfy Dobby's sexual needs.
New Year's Eve: It's New Year's Eve, and Mark is depressed about Dobby, but Jeremy is determined that the 'El Dude Brothers' are going to enjoy the night of their lives.
Luke's derriere disaster proves to be a two-man job for Sketch and Jay, Alice covers a design that reminds Katie of her ex, and Glen puts a snowman on ice.

Cindy Galardi Culpepper, the CEO and chairperson of Wienerschnitzel, the world's largest hot dog chain, goes incognito among her staff to look at the company's communication.
Lowell Hawthorne, the president and CEO of Caribbean food producer Golden Krust, goes undercover among the workforce in his own company, to determine the state of the business.
...Selling: Sheryl and Frank's renovations may be the least of the brothers' problems. Instead, earning Frank's trust proves to be as tough as nails.
Three couples compete to host the best dinner party in and around Newcastle. There's Scottish fare and assumptions about accents, and a dessert nearly goes up in flames!
In Manchester, Raf and Kevin serve up a 'healthy' menu featuring chocolate cake, Chantel and Stephen host a backyard party with hot tub fun, and Matthew and Jane dish up Asian cuisine.
The One with the Bear Grylls Groom: Survival expert Tom's only thinking of one thing for his wedding to fiancée Sue: a rugged, outdoor affair amidst the elements on a Scottish island.
The One in a Shopping Centre: Kelly's dream was to be a pro dancer, but her aspirations were cut short by illness. Fiancé David is planning a vibrant wedding with a dancing flash mob.
Country music artist Darius Rucker goes undercover at an open mic night, as a roadie and a busker, in a bid to find fresh songwriting and performing talent.
Restaurateur Marcus Samuelsson dons a disguise to work incognito in a teaching kitchen, a food truck and a culinary institute, searching for undiscovered chefs to mentor.
Mama Rita's: Gordon tries to bring new ideas to Mama Rita's Mexican restaurant in Newbury Park, southern California.
Le Bistro: Gordon visits high-end Le Bistro in Florida. Owner Andy has cooked for top chefs in the past, but he's lost his passion - and he doesn't respond well to criticism.
...and Selling: Brand new series: David and Siobhan keep getting outbid in their city's intense market. What tricks do Jonathan and Drew have up their sleeves to secure a sale?
Bit of an Ick: Anthony spirals into a place he may not be able to come back from. Dylan faces the music. And are Barbie and Kyle more than just friends?
The race for glory heats up as we reach the business end of the series. Bridget Christie researches Welsh royalty, and Judi Love pokes a shoe under a shower curtain.
Jimmy Carr hosts as Jonathan Ross and Russell Kane take on Alan Carr and Judi Love. Josh Jones joins Susie Dent in Dictionary Corner. With Rachel Riley.
Jimmy Carr hosts as Alan Carr and Harriet Kemsley play against Jonathan Ross and Maisie Adam. Huge Davies joins Susie Dent in Dictionary Corner. With Rachel Riley.
Seasonal Beatings: It's Christmas Day and Mark has invited his parents over for lunch. He's planned everything, but Jeremy is over-excited, and Dobby and Super Hans show up.
Jeremy Therapised: Mark has asked Dobby to move in with him, but Jeremy is dragging his heels over moving out.
